summary: This clipped page is a collection of R base package help pages (version 3.6.2) from RDocumentation, covering Bessel functions, built-in constants, operator syntax and precedence, integer vectors, and file.path. Each section gives the usage, arguments, return values, details, references and examples for its topic. Navigation, DataCamp links and boilerplate are omitted.
one_line: A compilation of R base 3.6.2 help pages on Bessel functions, built-in constants, operator precedence, integer vectors and file.path.
key_facts: The Bessel help page describes Bessel functions of integer and fractional order, of first and second kind (J_nu and Y_nu) and modified Bessel functions I_nu and K_nu.
The functions besselI, besselK, besselJ and besselY take arguments x (numeric, >= 0), nu (order, may be fractional and negative) and expon.scaled (logical, default FALSE).
For nu < 0, the Bessel help page says formulae 9.1.2 and 9.6.2 from Abramowitz & Stegun are applied, which is probably suboptimal, except for besselK which is symmetric in nu.
The Bessel help page warns that current algorithms give warnings about accuracy loss for large arguments and are rarely useful for nu in the order of millions.
The built-in constants are LETTERS, letters, month.abb, month.name and pi.
The Constants help page cites John Machin (ca 1706) who computed pi to over 100 decimal places using a Taylor series expansion.
The operator precedence list places :: and ::: highest, followed by $ and @, indexing, exponentiation (right to left), unary minus and plus, and the sequence operator ':'.
On the Syntax help page, assignment operators <- and <<- are right to left, '=' is also right to left, and ?' is help.
The Syntax help page notes that '=' has lower precedence than '<-', so x <- y = 5 gives a non-catchable error.
The integer help page says as.integer truncates non-integral numeric values towards zero and returns NA for real values larger in modulus than the largest integer.
The integer help page states that current implementations of R use 32-bit integers, restricting representable integers to about plus or minus 2 x 10^9.
The file.path help page says file.path constructs a path from components in a platform-independent way and returns an empty character vector if any argument has zero length, unlike paste.
The file.path help page says the function is designed to be faster than paste because it is used extensively in R itself.
The Bessel references include Abramowitz and Stegun (1972), Handbook of Mathematical Functions, Dover, New York, Chapter 9.
